headline: Tariff refunds drive a profit rebound despite soft revenue
summary_short: NOV's Q2 2026 revenue of $2,134M was up 4.0% sequentially but down 2.5% year-over-year, while net income rose to $112M ($0.31 diluted EPS) as operating profit jumped 35% y/y on roughly $40M of tariff refunds.
summary_long: Energy Equipment revenue rose 1% y/y on strong offshore project execution and richer mix; Energy Products and Services fell 5% y/y on lower capital equipment sales tied to Middle East disruption, partly offset by drill-bit/artificial-lift share gains and digital growth. Operating profit ($193M, +35% y/y) and Adjusted EBITDA ($283M, +$31M y/y) both benefited from a ~$40M tariff-refund credit. Net income was $112M ($0.31 diluted EPS, +$0.02 y/y); the effective tax rate rose to 26.1% from 0.9% a year ago, capping growth. Cash fell to $1,164M from $1,552M, on -$9M operating cash flow, $130M of H1 buybacks, and $97M of H1 dividends. Backlog was $4.08B, down $220M y/y. No forward guidance was issued this quarter.

drivers.explanation: Second-quarter revenue rose 4% sequentially and profitability jumped y/y, driven mainly by an approximately $40M combined tariff-refund benefit and stronger offshore project execution in Energy Equipment.

Y/y decline driven by Energy Products and Services (-5%) on lower capital equipment sales impacted by the Middle East conflict, partially offset by Energy Equipment (+1%) strength in offshore production equipment.
Gain reflects strong offshore production project execution, a more favorable sales mix in Energy Equipment, and an approximately $40M combined tariff-refund benefit across both segments.

Net income grew only modestly versus the large operating-profit gain because the effective tax rate rose to 26.1% from 0.9% a year ago, when a reserve release for unrecognized tax benefits had lowered the prior-year rate.
Operating cash flow swung to -$9M for H1 2026 from +$326M in H1 2025, primarily on changes in working capital — receivables, inventories, accounts payable, and accrued liabilities.
